newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican protesters attempt to disrupt Congress.
newsitem.headline: Mexican protesters attempt to disrupt Congress.

text.p: A group of protesters stormed the Mexican Congress on Wednesday and clashed with security guards, a week after the same group stripped naked before the lawmakers.

A handful of fired street cleaners threw potted plants and fought with security guards after forcing their way into the building, witnesses said. Police said late on Wednesday that 25 people were injured in the melee.
Trouble flared after the men arrived with Senator Felix Salgado of the leftist Democratic Revolutionary Party and demanded to be let into the legislative chamber.
Security guards prevented the men from entering the chamber and fighting broke out.

The skirmish was the latest event in an increasingly bitter and bizzare struggle by streetsweepers who say they were fired last year by the Tabasco state government for refusing to do unpaid, off-duty jobs for controversial Gov. Roberto Madrazo and other officials.
The cleaners' protest has gained national attention and become an embarrasment for President Ernesto Zedillo.

Two of the cleaners on Wednesday completed their 93rd day without food and were very close to death, doctors said. Five others finished their 45th day on a hunger strike. All of them were camped out under a thin plastic tent in front of the National Human Rights Commission.

The drama has also taken on a lighter note at times. Last week, fellow cleaners stormed Congress in their underwear and, in a show of solidarity to their striking compatriots, stormed the stage and dropped their underpants.

Late on Wednesday, representatives of the cleaners met with officials at the Interior Ministry to try to negotiate a solution to the strikers' demands that they be given back their jobs and paid compensation, officials said.
